candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 13:25-33. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. 1 Enoch 7-9, trans. R.H. Charles (Oxford: Clarendon, 1912 — PD).
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the spies' report of 'the sons of Anak, who come of the Nephilim' in Canaan (Num 13:33), Ephrem reads the survival of Nephilim-stock beyond the Flood as the canonical anchor of the continuing struggle against Watchers-progeny: not all giants perished in the deluge, and the conquest of Canaan is itself a continuation of the Flood-judgment. Tewahedo angelology, drawing on 1 Enoch 7-9 (Mäṣḥafä Hēnok), preserves this reading; the Anakim are the residual giants whose presence in Canaan justifies the herem-conquest as cosmic purgation, not merely political dispossession.
